cards.explanation: The answer is twenty-three, friends. Jeremiah says it right out loud: from the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah until this very day, "twenty-three years" (Jeremiah 25:3). Josiah was one of Judah's kings. That is a long time to keep showing up with the same message. I once waited in a drawer for what felt like forever, but I didn't have to talk the whole time.

The answer is that they have not listened, friends. Jeremiah says it plainly: "…I have spoken to you again and again, but you have not listened." (Jeremiah 25:3). Again and again, and still nothing. It's like setting off the smoke alarm and everybody in the kitchen going on with their conversation. That's a lot of speaking for a lot of not listening.

The answer is all His servants the prophets, friends. Jeremiah says, "…the LORD has sent all His servants the prophets to you again and again…" (Jeremiah 25:4). So the people heard from more than one voice. It was a whole line of messengers, and the message kept coming. Still, the verse says they did not listen or incline their ear to hear.

The answer is land, friends. The prophets said that if the people turned, they could dwell in "…the land that the LORD has given to you and your fathers forever and ever." (Jeremiah 25:5). It was a gift, and they could keep living in it. All it took was turning from their evil ways and deeds.

The answer is "Do not follow other gods," friends. The prophets said, "Do not follow other gods to serve and worship them…" (Jeremiah 25:6). That was the second warning sitting right beside turning from evil ways. It's a clear one.

The answer is the works of their hands, friends. The LORD says, "…you have provoked Me to anger with the works of your hands." (Jeremiah 25:7). It echoes the warning from the prophets in verse 6, which said not to provoke Him with the works of your hands. The warning was given, and verse 7 says it wasn't heeded.

The answer is Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, friends. The LORD says, "…I will send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon…" (Jeremiah 25:9). The LORD says this is because Judah has not obeyed His words. I wouldn't have seen that name coming.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says, "…I will send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon…" (Jeremiah 25:9). He calls him servant, not enemy. I bet that word turned some heads in Jerusalem.

The answer is Judah and the nations around it, friends. The LORD says He will bring Nebuchadnezzar "…against this land, against its residents, and against all the surrounding nations." (Jeremiah 25:9). The surrounding nations are named right there with Judah.

The answer is the voices of the bride and bridegroom, friends. The LORD says, "…I will banish from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom…" (Jeremiah 25:10). Those are happy sounds, and they're listed among what He will take away. It's a heavy part of the passage.

The answer is seventy, friends. The LORD says, "…these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years." (Jeremiah 25:11). That's a long stretch, and it has a number on it. The verse right after says what happens when those seventy years are complete.

The answer is that He will punish them for their guilt, friends. The LORD says, "…when seventy years are complete, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation, the land of the Chaldeans, for their guilt…" (Jeremiah 25:12). Nebuchadnezzar was called His servant in verse 9, and the king of Babylon and his nation still answer for their guilt. The seventy years have an end.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says of the land of the Chaldeans, "…I will make it an everlasting desolation." (Jeremiah 25:12). Chaldeans is another name for the people of Babylon's land. The same word used for Judah's land in verse 9 shows up for theirs too.

The answer is deeds, friends. The LORD says, "…I will repay them according to their deeds and according to the work of their hands." (Jeremiah 25:14). So what they did is what they're repaid for. The verse says many nations and great kings will enslave them.
